doc.title: Jerry Coker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 18, 2023

title: Supportive family, older brother, and teachers
summary: Parents were proud of his career, his older brother paved the way, and he studied with teachers such as Junie Ferrell.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes. But he was not a musician but he was very encouraging to my career. Were your parents happy that you were going to pursue music as a career?

Yes I think they were. They were really proud of it. And my older brother, he’s 3-1/2 years older than I was, sort of paved the way because I was always in his shadow for a long time now. He was a very good player and he was older, he had a little more experience and so, you know, it was helpful to have him around. So I had parents who appreciated what I was doing, and an older brother who was looking after me to make sure I was exposed to the right things and could answer questions when I had them. Eventually it turned around to where he would ask me things, you know, but it took a © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
while. Because he was a smart person. He had a very high grade average in school and in universitites.
Now when you went to college did you go as a — to study music because there was no jazz to be studied, but did you go then as a classical musician?

Well I was prepared to be a classical musician if necessary. And the courses, well for one thing I had private teachers who taught jazz that were good players. Junie Ferrell for example. I studied with him for quite some time. And it was a tremendous help. You know it kept me on track.
